skill.name: multi-agent-orchestration
skill.description: Route AI tasks across Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and Ollama with provider-specific delegation guidance.
skill.summary: Choose the right AI provider for each task and manage multi-agent delegation workflows.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown examples, placeholder API key names, or localhost development URLs. The remaining confirmed risk comes from intentional provider orchestration: local files can be expanded into cloud model prompts, and the skill documents external command delegation paths.

remediation.issue: Cloud examples read local files directly into provider prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent checks, file scope limits, and redaction guidance before any Gemini, Codex, Cursor, or OpenCode delegation.

remediation.issue: Full auto-approval mode is documented with only a brief warning.
remediation.suggestion: Require sandbox verification and user confirmation before recommending auto-approval or full-auto execution modes.

remediation.issue: Direct orchestration script examples pass task text to external provider adapters.
remediation.suggestion: Document quoting, prompt sanitization, and minimum required context for every provider execution command.

semantic_findings.title: Cloud Delegation Can Expose Sensitive Source Code
semantic_findings.description: The skill warns not to send sensitive data without consent, but Gemini examples include reading local source files into prompts for a cloud provider. Users need stronger scoping and consent guidance before cloud delegation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly recognizes sensitive-data risk and also gives examples that bulk-read local files into Gemini prompts. This is intended functionality rather than malware, so severity is medium.

semantic_findings.title: Auto-Approval Mode Requires Stronger Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The Codex cookbook documents full auto-approval mode and only says to use it in sandboxed environments. If copied into a non-sandboxed workflow, it can approve unintended commands without user review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The line documents a powerful auto-approval flag and includes a warning, but the guardrail is brief. The risk depends on user environment, so confidence is high enough to keep as a medium finding.

content.value_statement: AI teams often waste time choosing the wrong provider for a task. This skill gives routing rules, provider cookbooks, and parallel execution patterns for structured delegation.
actual_capabilities: Maps task types to Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, or Ollama providers.
Provides provider-specific setup, authentication, and delegation command examples.
Explains when to keep work in Claude Code instead of delegating.
Shows patterns for launching and collecting results from parallel agents.
Documents model tier selection for speed, cost, and task complexity.
Includes response handling templates for delegated agent results.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not install or configure provider CLIs.
Several examples require external provider accounts, subscriptions, or API keys.
Delegating sensitive data to cloud providers still requires explicit user consent.
Model names and provider capabilities can become stale over time.

use_cases.title: Select a provider for a coding task
use_cases.description: Route a code review, refactor, or implementation task to the provider with the best fit.

use_cases.title: Coordinate parallel research agents
use_cases.description: Plan multiple agents with different search angles and collect useful partial results.

use_cases.title: Keep private work local
use_cases.description: Use Ollama guidance when sensitive data should stay on the local machine.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the best provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the multi-agent orchestration skill to decide which provider should handle this task: [describe task]. Explain the routing choice before delegating.

prompt_templates.title: Delegate a large context task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the provider matrix to route this large context task. Check whether Gemini is appropriate, list any privacy concerns, and prepare a concise delegation prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Run local private analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Ollama local cookbook to plan a private analysis workflow for these files. Do not send content to cloud providers without my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Design a parallel agent plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a parallel agent plan for [research goal]. Assign distinct agent roles, model tiers, timeouts, and result collection rules.

output_examples.input: Route a task that needs video analysis and current web context.
output_examples.output: Recommended provider: Gemini. It supports multimodal inputs and web grounding. Confirm data sharing is acceptable before sending files.

output_examples.input: Plan parallel research on a new API migration.
output: Launch documentation, examples, changelog, and risk agents together.
Use fast models for discovery and a stronger model for synthesis.
Collect partial results after the timeout and report coverage gaps.

output_examples.input: Analyze proprietary code without cloud upload.
output_examples.output: Recommended provider: Ollama local. Use a local coding model and summarize results without exposing source code to external providers.

best_practices: Confirm provider availability and authentication before delegation.
Get user consent before sending sensitive files to cloud providers.
Launch independent agents in one parallel batch when speed matters.
anti_patterns: Do not delegate tasks that require hidden conversation history.
Do not use auto-approval modes outside a sandboxed environment.
Do not send entire repositories to external providers without scope control.

faq.question: Does this skill run agents by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides routing guidance and command examples. The user or orchestrator still executes the chosen workflow.

faq.question: Which providers are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers Claude, OpenAI Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and local Ollama.

faq.question: Can it handle sensitive data?
faq.answer: It can route sensitive work to local Ollama, but cloud delegation requires explicit consent and careful scoping.

faq.question: Why include model tier guidance?
faq.answer: Model tier guidance helps balance cost, speed, and reasoning quality across multi-agent workflows.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: Some provider cookbooks require API keys or subscriptions. Claude Code and local Ollama may use different authentication paths.

faq.question: Is this safe for automatic marketplace installation?
faq.answer: It should be reviewed because it includes external command examples, cloud delegation, and auto-approval guidance.
